problems.title: Bilinear stencil sampling does not implement the patch-wide rule
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, PDF p.6; unproject.py, interpolate_depth, lines 54–67
claim: The paper computes patch-mean depth and skips the \(3\)-D feature when over \(90\%\) of the patch is masked; the release downsamples depth and mask bilinearly.
analysis: At a \(14\)-to-\(1\) reduction with align_corners false, a patch output samples only its four central pixels, each weight \(1/4\). One valid central depth \(2\) among \(196\) pixels gives interpolated mask \(1/4>0.1\), so the release retains it despite \(195/196>0.9\) missingness. If only the four central pixels are invalid and the other \(192\) have depth \(2\), it rejects a mostly valid patch. With every pixel valid, central depth \(2\) and other depths \(4\), the patch mean is \(776/196\approx3.959184\), but the release gives \(2\). Both mask examples avoid ambiguity over averaging zero placeholders; the full-valid example avoids missing data entirely.
result: The stated complete-patch mean/missingness operation and active release differ. Constant/full-invalid controls agree, and no action failure or dataset prevalence is inferred.
repair: For aligned patches compute \(n_P=\sum M_p\) and \(u_P=\sum M_pD_p\). Retain when \(n_P>0\) and \(10n_P\ge A\), and use \(u_P/n_P\). This restores the declared local rule for the stated partition; changed checkpoints/performance require separate evaluation.
